title: spec review: S2c stable prompt prefixes: packet sections ordered stable then semi-stable then dynamic under [cache].prefix_mode shadow, role templates audited, prefix reuse measured (P7)
spec:
Audit and reorder packet construction in orchestrator/spawn.py (_packet_body and the role templates in .orchestrator/prompts/*.md). Classify every section: stable across tasks of a role (rules text in the templates, verify lines, tool-budget module, skills catalog ids), semi-stable per goal (base branch and goal, constraints, HOT memory lines), dynamic per task (objective, acceptance, write_scope, read_scope, relevant_tests, symbols, evidence, timestamps). New order when [cache].prefix_mode is active: stable block first (template rules moved above the packet placeholder inside each template, so the placeholder sits after the rules), then semi-stable, then dynamic; content of each section unchanged. prefix_mode (off|shadow|active, add as shadow with a dated comment). Shadow: build the legacy order for the worker but also compute the reordered text and record in packet_meta prefix_sha_legacy, prefix_sha_stable, prefix_chars_stable (the stable+semi-stable size) so cache_telemetry.report can show reuse_rate for both orders; active: worker receives the reordered packet. Never change acceptance, scope or rule wording. Also document in docs/hermes-hardening/09-stable-prefixes.md the per-role launch differences that break cross-run caching today (per-role --mcp-config, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools lists from spawn.py) and which are unavoidable. Extend scorecard --cache with a prefix table: per role, distinct prefixes and reuse_rate for legacy vs stable order over the window.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_prefix_active_orders_stable_before_dynamic (stable sections precede objective; section contents byte-identical to legacy)

risks.issue: record_run copies packet_meta into the persisted run row through a hardcoded allowlist of keys (lines 299-310, only 'prefix_sha, prefix_chars, suffix_chars, dynamic_sections' for the existing prefix mechanism). cache_telemetry.annotate/report read prefix data from that persisted row['context'], not from the task-level packet_meta dict. New keys prefix_sha_legacy, prefix_sha_stable, prefix_chars_stable will not reach run-row telemetry (and so test_report_prefix_table_legacy_vs_stable) unless this allowlist is extended, but orchestrator/bus.py is not in scope.

_record_prefix_identity (already landed, tests/test_spawn.py:51-74) already computes a 'legacy order' prefix hash: it hashes the template text preceding the packet's 'packet v<hash>' header line and stores it as prefix_sha/prefix_chars/dynamic_sections, already consumed by cache_telemetry.report's existing distinct_prefix_sha/reuse_rate columns and scorecard --cache. The spec never references this shipped mechanism and asks for a new, separately-named prefix_sha_legacy alongside prefix_sha_stable, risking two divergent 'legacy prefix' concepts and an inconsistent scorecard (existing top-level reuse_rate vs the new prefix table's legacy column).

packet() always prepends 'packet v<hash of full body> base <merge-base sha> sources ...' before the body, and that header line is exactly the prefix/suffix boundary _record_prefix_identity already uses. Reordering sections inside _packet_body (objective/acceptance/base/constraints/etc.) sits entirely inside the 'suffix' after that header and therefore cannot extend any real literal cache-eligible prefix beyond what moving template rules above {{packet}} already achieves. prefix_sha_stable as specced would measure a byte range that is never actually contiguous with the real stable prefix of a transmitted prompt; the spec and docs/09-stable-prefixes.md should say this is a shadow/projected comparison metric, not an achievable prefix, or scorecard consumers will overread it as real cache reuse.

The spec classifies 'HOT memory lines' as a semi-stable packet section to reorder, but _packet_body's sections list (lines 620-634: objective, acceptance, base, write_scope, read_scope, constraints, relevant_tests, symbols, gotchas, decisions, verify, evidence) has no HOT-memory section; memory_hot.py's generated output is not wired into packet construction anywhere. There is nothing to reorder for this classification as stated.

challenge.md and fix-round.md are in scope for 'template rules moved above the packet placeholder', but neither file contains a {{packet}} placeholder: challenge.md has no packet section at all, and fix-round.md uses a different single-brace {field} substitution mechanism with its own held-task failure context. The reordering instruction is inapplicable to these two files as written.

suggested_spec_changes: Add orchestrator/bus.py to scope and require extending record_run's packet_meta allowlist (~line 309) with prefix_sha_legacy, prefix_sha_stable, prefix_chars_stable so the new fields actually reach persisted run rows and cache_telemetry.report.

Require the implementation to reconcile with the already-shipped _record_prefix_identity/prefix_sha mechanism from T-1143 (either treat prefix_sha_legacy as an alias of the existing prefix_sha or explicitly define how the two differ), and update cache_telemetry's existing distinct_prefix_sha/reuse_rate columns to stay consistent with the new legacy-vs-stable prefix table.
Drop 'HOT memory lines' from the semi-stable classification (or scope in wiring memory_hot output into _packet_body as a prerequisite change) since no such packet section currently exists.

Narrow the per-template reordering behavior to execute.md/review.md/scout.md/spec-review.md, the four templates that actually contain {{packet}}; either drop challenge.md and fix-round.md from scope or state explicitly that prefix_mode is a no-op for them.

Have docs/hermes-hardening/09-stable-prefixes.md state plainly that packet-body-internal reordering cannot extend the real literal cache prefix past the packet's per-task header line, and that prefix_sha_stable is a shadow/projected comparison signal rather than an achievable cache boundary.
